messages:
maya: Heads up — eu-west3 gnode-24 just hit a sustained write IOPS spike during batch window, causing ephemeral cleaner to fanout tombstone deletions and blow past our writeq. Saw ~230k tombstones churn in 6m.

sam: Ugh. Did it also cause GPU allocs to fail?

maya: Yes, several GPU provisioning requests timed out, ops-oncall page fired. Provisioning backlog grew ~18s avg.

leo: Any correlation with thermal throttles on the NVMe? Recent firmware put a more aggressive temp watermark.

maya: Temp was fine (36C), so not thermal. I/O queue depth got saturated — kernel showed writeback backlog and high merge latency.

arjun: Paste of scrub logs: 
```
[2026-03-19T22:38:02Z] ephemeral-cleaner: plan delete tombstones=230412 batch=1024 iter=225 time=5m32s
[2026-03-19T22:38:02Z] writeq: queued=120k depth=256 inflight=240k
[2026-03-19T22:39:10Z] device nvme0n1: write latency p99=2.8s p999=9.4s
```

sam: Thanks. Could be a pathological fanout pattern — cleaner is trying to delete many tiny files which amplifies metadata ops.

maya: Confirmed — metadata ops/sec spiked far higher than block writes. nvmetop shows high fsync/sec and inodes churn.

reclaim-bot: Scheduled reclaim job started on gnode-24 (eu-west3) — plan: rate-limit deletes to 5k/s; probe window 30s. :robot_face:

leo: Can we apply a soft-rate limiter on the cleaner for that node pool immediately? We should avoid global param changes.

arjun: I pushed a per-node limiter to the janitor config: 
```
janitor:
  per_node_delete_rate: 5000
  backoff_multiplier: 1.5
  max_concurrent_batches: 8
```

ops-oncall: Applied to eu-west3 pool. Watching for decreased writeq and reclaimed CPU on kubelet. :eyes:

maya: After limiter, writeq depth dropped to ~40k, p99 latency down to 180ms. GPU provisioning resumed, backlog cleared in ~90s.

sam: Nice. For follow-up: we need an eval of tombstone distribution — if deletes are concentrated on few devices they still saturate metadata. Suggest split deletes across igroups.

leo: Also propose adding a cheap pre-check in cleaner to coalesce adjacent tombstones into chunked deletes (reduce xattrs/fsyncs). Low-risk feature flag.

arjun: I'll prototype chunked-delete and a probe that measures metadata ops/sec before aggressive fanout. If ops/sec > 50k, fall back to rate-limited mode.

maya: Cost note — this kind of churn increases tail IOPS and can force us into larger reserved capacity to meet SLOs. If we can reduce fanout, we can avoid buying extra short-term nvme headroom.

sam: Agreed. Also add an alert: "ephemeral.tombstone.fanout_ratio" when tombstones_deleted / bytes_written > 1000 over 5m. That will catch pathological metadata storms.

reclaim-bot: Created ticket INFRA-8273: "Chunked-delete for ephemeral cleaner + per-node rate limiting" and attached logs.

maya: Thanks. For immediate mitigation, thumbs up to keep per-node limiter and monitor for 24h. Will follow up with a postmortem if it recurs. :thumbsup:
